metadata.title: Shop closed after 90,000 cigarettes and illicit goods seized in police crackdown
metadata.contentSnippet: Police have closed down March Shop amid a major crackdown across Cambridgeshire which saw thousands of pounds worth of illicit goods seized.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Shop closed after 90,000 cigarettes and illicit goods seized in police crackdown
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Police have closed down a shop amid a major crackdown across Cambridgeshire which saw thousands of pounds worth of illicit goods seized. Officers joined local authorities and Immigration Enforcement for visits across Peterborough and Fenland in a three-week operation in October to tackle the sale of illegal goods and other criminality. They visited 60 businesses including convenience stores, barber shops, vape shops and hand car washes. Officers confiscated 764 vapes, 562 Nico pods, nearly 15kg of hand-rolling tobacco, and more than 90,000 cigarettes. More than 90,000 cigarettes were seized (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) The action was part of a wider effort to tackle money laundering and the grey economy linked to organised immigration crime like illegal working and human trafficking. March Shop in High Street, March, was hit with a closure order at Cambridge Magistrates' Court on November 13, with entry prohibited to everyone except for the landlord, their agents, emergency services, and employees of Fenland District Council. Whittlesey Local Store in Market Street, Whittlesey, has also been partially closed until February 13, with the condition that no vapes, tobacco or nicotine-related items are to be stored or sold anywhere on the premises. Whittlesey Local Store (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Detective Inspector Sarah Morgan said: "This was a successful operation that has resulted in a large number of illegal goods being taken off the streets. "The other forms of criminality associated with the sale of illicit goods have an adverse effect on the communities it happens within and is something we remain committed to tackling. Police were tackling the sale of illegal goods and other criminality (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) "We will continue to collaborate with partner agencies to protect the community by ensuring the businesses in our community operate lawfully." Two closure orders have been granted so far (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) During the inspections, 62 staff members completed modern slavery questionnaires and all reported being satisfied with their working conditions. Investigations are now underway into multiple offences, and closure orders are being sought for 10 shops found to be selling illegal goods. The operation also included visits to businesses in St Neots, supported by Huntingdonshire District Council. Officers visited St Neots (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) No items were seized there, and identified concerns are being dealt with by the relevant agency. The enforcement activity formed part of Operation Machinize, an ongoing project coordinated by the National Crime Agency to tackle money laundering and criminal use of cash-intensive high street businesses. The crackdown was part of a major operation (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) The operation was supported by GentiumUK K9 Operations Limited, who provided dogs trained for tracking and detecting narcotics, cash, and tobacco. Specially trained dogs aided the operation (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Councillor Susan Wallwork, Fenland District Council’s portfolio holder for community safety, said: "We are pleased to support the police and partner agencies in this operation and the ongoing efforts to tackle illegal activity and the harm it can cause in our communities. "By working together, we can help keep illegal goods off our streets and create safer places for everyone."

metadata.title: Rare Royal Mint 50p coin selling for more than 600 times its face value
metadata.contentSnippet: The rare Royal Mint 50p coin has sold for £330 on eBay, and there are thousands more out there that could be worth a small fortune

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Rare Royal Mint 50p coin selling for more than 600 times its face value
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: We are all being urged to check our change for a rare 50p coin after one sold for more than 650 times its face value at auction this week. The coin, a Kew Gardens 250 th anniversary coin, sold for £330 on eBay. It is one of the Royal Mint’s rarest and most valuable coins, with just 210,000 copies entering circulation when it was released in 2009. As a result, it is one of the most sought-after coins by collectors in the UK. The coin features the Chinese Pagoda at the Royal Botanic Gardens on the tails side and a portrait of the Queen. After being listed on online auction site eBay, the 50p coin attracted 14 bids before selling for £330.01. The 50 pence piece has become the most valued and collected coin in the UK, with many collectable designs appearing on its heptagonal canvas. Its 27.5mm diameter makes it the largest of any British coin, and allows space for decorative pictures. It has often been used to celebrate big events over the past 50 years of British history. The rarest coins tend to be of the greatest value, with the mintage (number of coins with each design made) being the fundamental attraction for collectors. Along with the design, other aspects of the coin which increase value are the condition of the coin and whether it has an error in its design. The way in which it is sold can also determine the coin’s value - while some coin collectors will bid vast amounts of money on eBay or at auction, others opt for more robust valuations by selling via a coin dealer. metadata.contentSnippet: A petition with more than 13,000 signatures wants passengers to face penalties if they refuse to make room for wheelchair users. Ministers have responded.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Passengers could be made to fold prams as Government reviews wheelchair access laws
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Wheelchair users could be given stronger legal protections when travelling by bus and coach, after the Government confirmed it is reviewing whether existing laws to safeguard spaces for disabled travellers need to change. The Department for Transport has responded to a petition calling for wheelchair users to have an enforceable right to designated spaces, regardless of the order in which passengers board. But, some passengers have said it is difficult for parents to fold up their prams on busy buses, so they also need to use wheelchair spaces. The petition, created by Isabel Canto, has attracted 13,496 signatures and can be signed until March 15, 2027. It calls for passengers without a competing disability-related or extenuating need to be required to move, share or fold their prams to make room for a wheelchair user. It also wants drivers to be required to enforce the rules, with penalties for passengers who refuse to comply. At present, wheelchair users can still be left unable to board if another passenger refuses to vacate the designated space. Responding on November 9, the Government acknowledged that, despite existing legal protections, wheelchair users can still face refusals and distressing confrontations when trying to travel. It said: "We recognise the petitioners' central concern that existing protections do not always provide wheelchair users with the certainty they need." The Government confirmed it has asked the Law Commission to review the existing legal framework for transport accessibility. Its findings will help Ministers consider whether legislation needs to change to better support disabled people travelling independently and with dignity. However, it stopped short of committing to the specific changes demanded by the petition. The response said any new rules would need to take account of other passengers who may also have access needs, including those whose disabilities or other protected characteristics mean they cannot easily move elsewhere on the vehicle. It added that any penalties would need to be practical and enforceable, while avoiding unsafe situations for drivers and passengers. The petition argues that access to wheelchair spaces should not depend on the goodwill of other passengers. Its wording states: "Passengers without a competing disability-related or extenuating need should be required to follow directions to move, share or fold belongings, with penalties for refusal." The Government said buses and coaches are an essential service for many disabled people, whose needs should be anticipated in the way services are designed and operated. Since 2000, the Public Service Vehicles Accessibility Regulations have required buses and coaches covered by the rules to include specific accessibility features, including at least one wheelchair space with accompanying signage. Drivers also have legal duties under separate regulations to facilitate access to a vacant wheelchair space and provide the required boarding assistance. The Equality Act 2010 additionally requires operators to make reasonable adjustments to avoid placing disabled people at a substantial disadvantage. The Government pointed to a 2017 Supreme Court ruling which clarified that reasonable adjustments can include a driver requiring passengers to move from a wheelchair space when it is needed by a wheelchair user, and taking further steps to persuade them where appropriate. Despite this, Ministers acknowledged that wheelchair users can still be denied access, disrupting journeys to work, education and social activities and undermining confidence in travelling independently. The Government also outlined wider plans to improve bus accessibility. These include requiring drivers and customer-facing staff to complete disability awareness and assistance training every five years, and making local transport authorities publish an accessibility plan for their bus networks at least every three years. It is also developing a Transport Accessibility Charter intended to support a more consistently accessible journey. Mumsnet users took to the parenting forum to raise the issue with pram folding, with one user starting a thread saying: "Do people really manage to fold their prams in busy buses?. In it, they said: "Technically I have a pram which can be folded with one hand and in a couple of seconds (according to the advert), but practically I also have a baby strapped in, a pram bag attached, a thousand loose items in the bottom and a hundred toys attached. "I just was asked to fold my pram because the bus got a bit busy, but after giving this a quick thought I realised that this would be somewhere between a circus number, comedy and horror show, so I just got off the bus. Are there some Supermamas who just say ‘sure’, clack and done, and if yes, where can I learn this skill, please?" Another responded: "Not that I’ve seen unless the child they have is old enough to sit on a seat while they painstakingly take it all apart / try to use the fold function. Generally people get off if there is a wheelchair or squeeze up if it gets busy." Recommended reading: Others offered tips: "Have a backpack bag and nothing loose in the bottom. I've asked someone seated nearby to hold the baby for a minute if necessary. Better to take a small buggy and fold before you get on though if possible." The petition has already passed the 10,000-signature threshold, triggering a Government response. If it reaches 100,000 signatures before it closes on March 15, 2027, it will be considered for debate in Parliament. Do you think the laws to protect accessible spaces should be stronger? Should parents be made to fold prams? Tell us in the comments below...

metadata.title: State Pension age change means 197,000 pensioners miss out on Winter Fuel Payment
metadata.contentSnippet: Winter Fuel Payments are due to start arriving this week, but an estimated 197,000 people will miss out because of the rising State Pension age.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: State Pension age change means 197,000 pensioners miss out on Winter Fuel Payment
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An estimated 197,000 pensioners will miss out on this winter's Winter Fuel Payment because of a change to the State Pension age, as payments begin arriving in bank accounts this week. People who turn 66 might assume they qualify for the annual payment, worth between £100 and £300. But the gradual rise in the State Pension age from 66 to 67 means reaching your 66th birthday is no longer enough. According to The Solar Co, around 197,000 people who turned 66 before the end of this year's qualifying week will miss out because they had not yet reached their State Pension age. The qualifying week ran from September 21 to September 27, 2026. Anyone born after June 27, 1960 does not meet the age requirement for this winter's payment. That means someone born on June 27 qualifies, while someone born just one day later does not – even though both will have turned 66 by the end of September. People born between June 28 and September 27, 1960 must wait until they are 66 years and three months old to reach State Pension age. George Penny, Home Energy Expert at The Solar Co, said: "The Winter Fuel Payment is a tax-free annual payment from the government that helps older people cover the cost of heating their homes during the colder months. The amount varies between £100 and £300, depending on your age and living circumstances. "Many people assume that turning 66 means they’ll get the Winter Fuel Payment, and until this year, that was true. But with the state pension age now rising, your 66th birthday is no longer the date that counts. "Someone born on 27 June 1960 qualifies this winter, while someone born the next day doesn’t, even though both turned 66 well before the qualifying week. "If you’re expecting your first payment, check your State Pension age before including it in your winter budget." The Government's eligibility rules confirm that people must have been born on or before June 27, 1960 to qualify for the 2026/27 Winter Fuel Payment, provided they meet the other conditions. Most eligible pensioners will receive their payment automatically in November or December. Those with a personal income above £35,000 will have the money reclaimed by HMRC through the tax system. Recommended reading: For households facing higher heating bills, George has also shared four ways to keep warm and make savings this winter. 1. Check what other support you could get Missing out on the Winter Fuel Payment does not necessarily mean you will be left without help. George said: "Missing out on the Winter Fuel Payment doesn’t mean you can’t get help elsewhere. The Warm Home Discount takes £150 off eligible households’ electricity bills this winter, and most people receive it automatically. "If you think you qualify but haven’t heard anything by the end of January, contact the Warm Home Discount helpline." 2. Heat the rooms you use rather than the whole house Rather than switching off the heating altogether, George recommends concentrating warmth in the rooms where you spend most of your time. He said: "Rather than cutting back on heating, focus it where you spend your time. Close doors to keep heat in, turn down thermostatic radiator valves in unused rooms, and keep your main living space at a comfortable temperature, ideally at least 18°C." 3. Use a heated throw instead of a plug-in heater A heated throw could cost around 8p to run for three hours, compared with approximately £1.58 for a typical plug-in heater over the same period, according to George. He said: "If you’re sitting still in the evening, heating the person is far cheaper than heating the room. Using a typical plug-in heater for three hours costs around £1.58, compared with just 8p for a heated throw. That’s a saving of £1.50 a night, or about £45 over a month of daily use. Costs vary depending on the model and setting, so check the label. Never leave a heated throw on unattended or use one that’s frayed or damaged." 4. Make the most of free warmth from the sun Opening curtains and blinds during daylight hours can help bring some natural warmth into your home, even on colder days. George said: "Even on a cold winter’s day, sunshine coming through a window can help warm a room at no cost. Open the curtains and blinds on south-facing windows when the sun is out, so the light can reach the room. "As soon as the light starts to fade, close them again to help keep that warmth in. Thick or lined curtains work best. Tuck them behind radiators rather than letting them hang over the top, so the heat goes into the room instead of towards the window."

metadata.title: Little-known UK airport rule that could see electronic devices confiscated
metadata.contentSnippet: If your electronic devices do not switch on if you are asked to turn them on by security, they can be taken away from you.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Little-known UK airport rule that could see electronic devices confiscated
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: If you are planning a winter getaway for the next coming weeks or already have a holiday booked for next summer, you might want to make sure you are aware of all of the airport rules you must follow. Most people travelling will at least be carrying a mobile phone with them and some might bring a laptop. Travellers are being warned about a little-known airport rule that can lead to your electronic devices like your phone being taken away. Your devices can be taken away if they do not switch on. (Image: Getty) The UK government has shared information about the hand luggage restrictions at UK airports. It says that travellers must have their devices charged and be able to switch them on when requested. The website reads: “Make sure your electronic devices are charged before you travel. “If your device does not switch on when requested, you will not be allowed to take it onto the aircraft.” If you cannot turn on your electronic device when asked by airport security, they have the right to confiscate it. This rule is not exclusive to British airports with many American and European airports also having the same rule in place. Airlines will allow passengers to take things like their mobile phones, laptops, and even electric shavers in their hand luggage and hold luggage. E-cigarettes are allowed in hand luggage but cannot be taken in hold luggage. The rules can vary between different airlines so you will want to check specific restrictions for your airline. If you have any lithium batteries, most airlines like easyJet and Ryanair will have strict rules on how these must be stored if you are bringing them with you. Many airlines say lithium batteries must be stored in your hand luggage rather than your checked baggage. Recommended reading Other items like cameras can be taken in both hold and checked luggage but there might be some restrictions on specialist equipment like professional video cameras. You can also take hair curlers that contain a gas cartridge on a plane as long as the safety cover is fitted on it at all times. Did you know your electronic devices had to be charged up at the airport? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Imperial Brands to axe up to 2,500 jobs by 2030 in savings drive
metadata.contentSnippet: Tobacco firm Imperial Brands is to cut up to 2,500 more jobs globally over the next four years as part of a major cost saving programme.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Imperial Brands to axe up to 2,500 jobs by 2030 in savings drive
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Tobacco firm Imperial Brands is to cut up to 2,500 more jobs globally over the next four years as part of a major cost saving programme. The JPS, Golden Virginia and Rizla owner said it comes on top of a shake-up which saw it slash around 2,100 roles in the year to September. The company said the transformation is part of a plan to secure at least £320 million in savings by 2030. The group reported a 1.5% decline in revenues to £31.7 billion for the year to September, compared with a year earlier. Imperial Brands is among tobacco firms to have been weighed down by a continued decline in cigarette volumes, but it reported further growth in demand for its “next generation products”, including vapes and oral tobacco. Lukas Paravicini, chief executive officer of the firm, said: “While continuing to invest in and build future consumer capabilities, underpinned by new technologies, we are confident of achieving at least £320 million of annual savings by 2030. “We have delivered annualised savings of £90 million, with actions taken since the programme began supporting future annualised savings of £180 million – more than half of our target.”

metadata.title: Paedophile jailed for 17 years after raping and sexually assaulting three children
metadata.contentSnippet: William Floyd jailed for 17 years after raping and sexually assaulting three children in Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Paedophile jailed for 17 years after raping and sexually assaulting three children
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A paedophile who raped and sexually assaulted three children has been jailed for a total of 17 years. William Floyd, 28, was sentenced for historic sexual assaults in Peterborough, with his crimes uncovered after a police investigation led to the discovery of indecent images of children on his mobile phone. During the investigation, officers also found evidence on the device of him discussing sexually assaulting children. Detective Constable Helen Keighley, who led the investigation, said: "William Floyd subjected his victims to horrific sexual assaults and the severity of his crimes are reflected in the sentence handed down. "I would like to pay tribute to the victims: their immense bravery and courage in coming forward to tell police about these abhorrent crimes has led to Floyd being removed from society for a long time." Floyd, of no fixed address, pleaded guilty to six counts of rape, five counts of sexual assault of a child, three counts of assault by penetration of a child, two counts of possessing indecent photographs of a child, and one count each of causing or inciting a child to engage in sexual activity, engaging in sexual activity in the presence of a child, and possession of an extreme pornographic image. He was sentenced on November 12 at Peterborough Magistrates’ Court, which was sitting as a crown court. Floyd was also ordered to sign the Sex Offenders Register indefinitely and was given an indefinite sexual harm prevention order, along with an indefinite restraining order against the victims. He will serve eight years and six months in custody, with the total sentence of 17 years coming from concurrent sentences and a licence period.

metadata.title: James Blunt to perform at Thetford Forest in 2027
metadata.contentSnippet: James Blunt will perform at Thetford Forest on June 18 next year as part of Forestry England’s Forest Live 2027.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: James Blunt to perform at Thetford Forest in 2027
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: James Blunt is set to return to the stage with special outdoor performance at Thetford Forest. The chart-topping singer-songwriter will perform on June 18, marking his first Forest Live appearance since 2014. The show is part of Forestry England's Forest Live concert series, held at unique woodland locations across the country. The English singer-songwriter rose to fame with his 2004 debut album Back to Bedlam, which became the UK’s best-selling record of the 2000s. It featured the global hit singles You’re Beautiful and Goodbye My Lover. He has since sold more than 20 million records and earned five Grammy nominations. Known for his sharp, self-deprecating humour on social media, Blunt recently reached new audiences as a fan-favourite contestant on The Celebrity Traitors, finishing in third place. The Thetford show will feature songs from his current number one album Airplane Mode. Support acts for the night include Nathan Evans & The Saint PHNX Band and Cassandra Coleman. Evans, a Scottish singer-songwriter, has teamed up with Glaswegian alt-pop/folk-rock duo Saint PHNX to create a sound that blends Scottish folk storytelling with contemporary rock and pop. Cassandra Coleman, an indie-folk-pop artist from Tennessee, gained national attention as a top-10 finalist on American Idol and is known for her cinematic vocals. She released her debut EP End of Your Love, which includes a collaboration with Jack Antonoff and Bleachers. Blunt joins a growing list of artists confirmed for Forest Live 2027, including Rudimental, who will also perform at Thetford Forest. Tickets for all Forest Live shows will go on general sale at 10am on Friday, November 20. Fans can sign up for updates and exclusive pre-sale access at www.forestlive.com.

metadata.title: Knifeman was 'hearing voices saying he was going to be attacked', court hears
metadata.contentSnippet: Anthony Williams, who is accused of attempted murder in an attack on an LNER train in Huntingdon last year was "hearing voices", a court heard.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Knifeman was 'hearing voices saying he was going to be attacked', court hears
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A knifeman accused of attempted murder in an attack on a train in Huntingdon last year was "hearing voices" and "believed he was going to be attacked", a court heard. Several people were injured on an LNER train from Doncaster to London King's Cross on November 1, 2025 which was forced to make an emergency stop in Huntingdon. Anthony Williams, 33, denies 14 counts of attempted murder: ten of them in relation to the LNER train, three said to have happened in Peterborough and one at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London. Dr Bernard Chin, a consulting forensic psychiatrist at North London NHS Foundation Trust, was cross-examined by Gillian Jones KC as the defence made their case at Cambridge Crown Court on November 17. Dr Chin assessed Williams shortly after the incident on the LNER train. The court heard that Williams said: "I was paranoid people were going to attack me, they were coming for me, cars were going to run me over. "I was hearing a lot of voices, feeling a lot of fear. "I was extremely paranoid, I knew people were after me, the cars were following me. "I went to the river because no cars could run me over there." Dr Chin told jurors that Williams had said he believed his house was bugged and he had been sleeping outside in the woods, but was still hearing voices. The court heard that the voices were reportedly getting worse by Halloween 2025. Dr Chin told the court that Williams said: "I was on TikTok asking for a sign and it showed a video of someone stabbing someone. "It was a warning to me. I needed to protect myself." The court heard that when Williams was on the LNER train, he said he continued to hear the voices. Dr Chin told jurors that Williams said: "I just kept hearing 'you are going to get attacked, they are going to kill you' through the speakers on the train. "I wasn't really thinking, at the time I just needed to protect myself. "It was me or them." The court heard that Dr Chin diagnosed Williams with schizophrenia, a diagnosis echoed by another professor. He told jurors he defined schizophrenia as a form of psychosis, where one is unable to tell reality and the inner world apart, describing it as a "severe and enduring mental illness". The court heard that while Williams was likely to have been intoxicated with alcohol, this was unlikely to have caused or sustained the psychosis, and the test for insanity was not met. Earlier this month, Williams pleaded guilty to 10 counts of wounding with intent relating to the incident on the LNER train, the wounding with intent of a man at Pontoon Dock DLR station in the early hours of November 1 and to the wounding with intent of a 14-year-old boy in Peterborough on October 31, as well as a number of other offences. The trial continues.

metadata.title: Huntingdon MP backs standalone council and warns split would be ‘a disaster’
metadata.contentSnippet: Huntingdon MP Ben Obese-Jecty has backed a standalone unitary authority for Huntingdonshire ahead of the Government’s decision on local government reform.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Huntingdon MP backs standalone council and warns split would be ‘a disaster’
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Huntingdon MP Ben Obese-Jecty has backed a standalone unitary authority for Huntingdonshire ahead of the Government’s decision on local government reform. Ben Obese-Jecty, MP for Huntingdon, met with Minister for Local Government Jim McMahon MP to make the case for a dedicated authority under Option E, warning that Option D, which would split Huntingdonshire in two, would be “a disaster” for communities and public services. Mr Obese-Jecty said: "Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) will shape how public services are delivered and how our communities are represented for generations to come, so it is vital that ministers get this right for Huntingdonshire. "While my views on LGR are already well documented through the debates I have led and the dozens of questions I have put to ministers in Parliament, meeting directly with Jim McMahon was a welcome opportunity to make our case face-to-face. "I set out clearly why Option E, a dedicated Huntingdonshire unitary authority, is the right choice to allow our area to thrive, and why Option D, which would carve Huntingdonshire in two, would be a disaster." The meeting took place ahead of the government’s next round of announcements on local government reorganisation, expected before Christmas. Mr Obese-Jecty has led Commons debates, challenged ministers and tabled dozens of written questions on the issue. He said: "With the next round of announcements due before Christmas and a formal response window to follow, I will continue to fight tooth and nail in Westminster to protect Huntingdonshire's identity and secure the best possible outcome for my constituents." After the Government announces its “minded-to” decision, local groups will have a formal chance to respond to its preferred option. This will not require a legal challenge, according to the latest Government guidance.

metadata.title: DWP State pensioners over 80 to get extra cash boost on top of £374 annual rise
metadata.contentSnippet: Pensioners aged over 80 may qualify for an extra State Pension payment on top of the £374 annual increase due from April 2027.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP State pensioners over 80 to get extra cash boost on top of £374 annual rise
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Many older state pensioners - aged over 80 - are in line for an extra cash boost to their weekly payments from April, on top of the annual increase confirmed under the triple lock. The additional payment is available to certain pensioners who reached State Pension age before April 2016 and are receiving the old basic State Pension. Unlike those who qualify for the newer State Pension system, older pensioners can receive an additional payment when they reach the age of 80, provided they meet the qualifying conditions. The change comes as millions of pensioners prepare for the next annual State Pension increase, which will take effect from April 2027. The basic State Pension is expected to rise by 3.9% under the triple lock, taking the weekly rate from £184.90 to £192.10. This represents an increase of £7.20 a week, or approximately £374 a year, for someone receiving the full basic State Pension. The triple lock guarantees that the State Pension rises each April by whichever is highest of inflation, average earnings growth or 2.5%. The Government has confirmed it will remain in place for the 2027/28 financial year. In a statement to parliament, DWP secretary Pat McFadden said: "I have concluded my statutory annual review of State Pension and benefit rates under the Social Security Administration Act 1992. The new rates will apply in the tax year 2027-28 and will mainly come into effect from 12 April 2027. "I am pleased to announce that the basic and full rate of the new State Pensions will be increased by 3.9%, in line with the increase in average weekly earnings in the year to May-July 2026. "This delivers on our Triple Lock commitment throughout this Parliament to increase these rates in line with the highest of growth in prices, growth in earnings or 2.5%. From April, the full annual rate of the new State Pension will increase by around £490. The full annual rate of the basic State Pension will increase by around £375." He later added: "Other State Pension and benefit rates covered by my statutory review will be increased by 3.5%, in line with the increase in the consumer prices index in the year to September 2026. This includes most working-age benefits and other benefits for people below State Pension age; benefits to help with additional needs arising from disability; Statutory Payments including Statutory Sick Pay and Statutory Maternity Pay; and Additional State Pension. The Pension Credit Savings Credit maximum amount will also increase by 3.5%." Recommended reading: The additional payment for people aged 80 and over is known as the over-80 pensio, or Serps. It is designed to provide extra support to older pensioners who receive a lower rate of State Pension under the previous system. The old basic State Pension was closed to new claims in April 2016, when the new State Pension system was introduced. People who reached State Pension age before that date generally receive the old basic State Pension, alongside any additional State Pension they built up through their National Insurance contributions. Those reaching State Pension age after April 2016 instead qualify under the new system, which has a higher maximum weekly rate and operates under different rules.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire school issues warning ahead of GTA VI release
metadata.contentSnippet: Longsands Academy in St Neots has issued a warning to parents ahead of the hotly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto (VI).

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire school issues warning ahead of GTA VI release
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A school in Cambridgeshire has issued a warning to parents ahead of the hotly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto (VI). Longsands Academy in St Neots has written to parents to "remind families" the game is "not intended for people of secondary school age." It comes after Rockstar Games confirmed the official launch timings for GTA VI, which is set to be released on Thursday November 19. The game will officially launch at 12am for players in the UK on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles. Astrea Academy Trust, which runs the school, said major game launches can "tempt some young people to try to take some time off school. A spokesperson said: "We have contacted parents about the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto VI, due for launch on Thursday November 19. "We are committed to promoting children’s wellbeing, help them to develop safe and healthy online habits and ensure that young people have every opportunity to learn at school. “With the release of this much anticipated game, we wanted to remind families that it carries an 18 certificate and is not intended for children or young people of secondary school age. "We have suggested to parents and carers to make use of the parental controls available on gaming devices and platforms, and to be aware of the content their children can access through shared consoles, family accounts and friends’ devices." They added: "Regular attendance is vital for children’s educational progress, wellbeing and future success. "We have reminded parents and carers that we expect all students to attend school as normal and that absence to play a video game would not be a reason to miss lessons." metadata.contentSnippet: Award-winning pizza restaurant chain Caprinos is set to open at St Benedicts Court in Huntingdon - with a free pizza party on launch day.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Award-winning pizza chain to open new Hunts restaurant with free pizza party
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An award-winning pizza restaurant chain is set to open in Huntingdonshire - with a free pizza party on launch day. Caprinos Pizza, which won Pizza Takeaway of the year in 2020 and 2022, will launch its latest branch at 16 St Benedicts Court, Huntingdon, on Wednesday, November 18. To mark the opening, the store will host a "Pizza Party" and offer a free 9-inch pizza to all walk-in customers between 5pm and 6pm on launch day. The chain has more than 100 stores across the UK, including in Cambridge, Bedford and London. Gul Nawaz and Khalil Rehman, co-founders of Caprinos Pizza, said: "We’re delighted to be bringing Caprinos to Huntingdon and introducing local customers to our combination of innovative flavours, high-quality ingredients and affordable prices. "From our signature pizzas to our Loaded Fries and desserts, we’re looking forward to giving people plenty of reasons to try something new. "Working closely with our local franchisee, we want the store to become a valued part of the Huntingdon community. "Our opening Pizza Party is a chance for customers to meet the team and try a pizza on us, and we can’t wait to welcome everyone through the doors." There will also be 50 per cent off all pizzas on November 18 and 19, followed by 25 per cent off everything from November 20 to 22. Caprinos Pizza is an award-winning chain (Image: Caprinos) A buy one get one free offer is also available during opening week on collection pizza orders. Caprinos’ menu features a range of pizzas including the Asian Classic Mix with tandoori chicken, Vegetarian Supreme, and the Caprinos Special which has spicy beef. The menu also includes sides, loaded fries, wraps, salads, desserts and milkshakes. Customers can try the brand’s Detroit Pizza format and newer flavours such as Chorizo Legend and Hot Honey Pesto, as well as chocolate dessert pizzas. Orders can be placed online now.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire lottery player has come forward to claim a £1 million Lotto prize after a search to track down the winner. The winning ticket was purchased in the Fenland district for the October 17 2026 draw. The ticket-holder matched five main numbers and the Bonus Ball in the Round 2 draw to secure the £1 million prize. The winning numbers were 4, 9, 15, 32, 38, 42 and the Bonus Ball was 2. Andy Carter, Senior Winners' Advisor at Allwyn, operator of The National Lottery, said: "There's nothing better than closing the chapter on an unclaimed prize and opening the door to a winner's future. "We're thrilled that the owner of this £1m Lotto ticket has come forward and can now start enjoying the life-changing impact of their win. "It's a wonderful outcome and exactly the news we were hoping for." The claim will now undergo a validation process to ensure all game rules and terms and conditions have been met. If validated, the prize will be paid at an appointment with one of Allwyn’s Winners’ Advisers. No details about the ticket-holder, including whether the winner is an individual or part of a syndicate, will be released unless they choose to go public. Winners of major prizes have the option to remain anonymous or share their story with the public. It is not known exactly where the winning ticket was bought.

metadata.title: WATCH: Paralympian Lauren Steadman MBE gives tour of new Hunts gym
metadata.contentSnippet: Paralympian Lauren Steadman MBE has given a tour of new Sawtry gym The Engine Room, which she has launched with her partner Bradley Chapman.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: WATCH: Paralympian Lauren Steadman MBE gives tour of new Hunts gym
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Paralympian Lauren Steadman MBE has given The Hunts Post a tour of the new Huntingdonshire gym she has launched with her partner, Navy boxer Bradley Chapman. The Engine Room opened at Brookside Industrial Estate in Sawtry on Monday, November 9, offering an open gym, Hyrox training and boxing classes. There is also an outdoor area complete with sauna, ice baths and changing rooms. The gym includes an outside wellness area complete with ice baths (Image: Lauren Steadman) Lauren, 34, who has won multiple Paralympic medals for Britain, competing in swimming and triathlon hopes her new project will see elite Olympians training alongside regular gym-goers. Alongside her is her partner Bradley Chapman, a former captain of the Royal Navy boxing team. Lauren was born in Peterborough and grew up in Sawtry, while Bradley grew up in Brampton. Bradley said: "We were sat in the kitchen and had a chat about how we wanted to move forward and how our future looked. "With my transition out of the Royal Navy I was thinking what do I see myself doing. "Coaching has been a massive part of my life, especially for the last several years and with Lauren training for the LA games, she needs a home for her training. "I'm from a boxing background and we had tried Hyrox so we thought why not merge the two worlds." The gym will be inclusive of all ages and abilities (Image: Lauren Steadman) Lauren said that they have had an "exceptional" response since the launch, considering the pair have only just relocated back to the area. She said: "We have signed up members already, the boxing classes have been thriving, the amount of juniors that have been coming through the door is incredible." Lauren said they have even had people up to 70 years old who want to maintain their strength coming in, as well as people who have been out of touch with sport for several years. She said: "I've also got a beautiful story of a young lad named Bertie who is missing an arm and lives locally. The Engine Room gym in Sawtry launched on Monday, November 9. (Image: Lauren Steadman) "His mum brought him in and he learned some tips and tricks from me, and that is what it's all about. "We want to remove the barriers, have no stigma around anything and there is space for absolutely anyone." Bradley said that their main priority is building a community and that they want to create "a real lasting memory" in the space. Lauren added: "We want people to be able to say that's my gym, that's where I train. "If we can provide that, where people come and just feel part of something, it will be pretty special."

metadata.title: Godmanchester community honours the fallen at remembrance service
metadata.contentSnippet: Godmanchester marked Remembrance Sunday on November 8 with a poignant war memorial ceremony led by Mayor Debbie Mickelburgh and Deputy Lieutenant Richard Pemberton.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Godmanchester community honours the fallen at remembrance service
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Residents gathered in Godmanchester to remember those who served. Councillor Debbie Mickelburgh, mayor of Godmanchester, and Richard Pemberton, deputy lieutenant of Cambridgeshire, led Sunday’s ceremony on November 8. They led town councillors, serving and former armed forces members, community representatives and children from local schools and groups in procession. Godmanchester Mayor Councillor Debbie Mickelburgh (left) and remembrance service attendees. (Image: Alan Hooker and Godmanchester Town Council) The group walked along Post Street with representatives from St Mary’s Church before reaching the town’s war memorial. Pastor Daniel Beckett of Godmanchester Baptist Church led the service, during which the Last Post was played and attendees reflected during a moment of silence. The Godmanchester Community Association fired poppy cannons in honour of those who served. The deputy lieutenant laid the first wreath, followed by the town mayor and serving and former armed forces members. The names of the fallen were then read aloud. Macebearers and Mr Richard Pemberton, Deputy Lieutenant of Cambridgeshire (middle) at the Godmanchester remembrance service. (Image: Alan Hooker and Godmanchester Town Council) Year 6 pupils from Godmanchester Community Academy and Godmanchester Bridge Academy read “Poppies for Remembrance” and “A Candle of Peace”. The community then sang “O God, Our Help in Ages Past”. The service ended with final blessings and the national anthem before the procession returned to Godmanchester Town Hall. Refreshments, including poppy-themed cupcakes donated by Eden Cupcake Floristry, were served at the Black Bull Pub in partnership with Godmanchester Town Council. The event brought the community together in a strong display of remembrance. A spokesperson for Godmanchester Town Council said: "It was fantastic to see so many Godmanchester residents join to remember and honour those who served our country." The ceremony showed Godmanchester’s continuing commitment to remembrance.

metadata.title: Robert Pattinson announced as the next actor to play James Bond
metadata.contentSnippet: Robert Pattinson has been officially announced as the next actor to play James Bond after a lengthy casting process

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Robert Pattinson announced as the next actor to play James Bond
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next actor to play James Bond. The 40-year-old was revealed in a series of Instagram posts on the official franchise account. It comes after a lengthy casting process in which several names were rumoured to be in the running for the role. This included the likes of Slow Horses star Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor and Nicholas Hoult. Pattinson succeeds Daniel Craig in the role, who last played the character in 2021's No Time to Die. In a statement reported by Variety, Pattinson said: "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. "I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. "To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. "I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team." Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next James Bond film and discussed Pattinson's casting. He shared: "Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. "We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. "I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. "He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin." Robert Pattinson is an English actor who began appearing in TV and film roles in 2004. He is best known for playing Edward Cullen in The Twilight Saga films, Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and Bruce Wayne/Batman in 2022's The Batman. Other major films he has appeared in include Tenet, Mickey 17, The Lighthouse and Die My Love. In 2026, Pattinson has featured in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, The Drama and Primetime, and he will also appear in Dune: Part Three as Scytale. metadata.title: Ready Steady Roll: award-winning café offers screen-free fun from £2
metadata.contentSnippet: Ready Steady Roll review: discover the welcoming Sharnbrook board game café near Kimbolton, with hundreds of games, food, drinks and sessions for all ages.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Ready Steady Roll: award-winning café offers screen-free fun from £2
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Kath Sansom recently visited Ready Steady Roll, which has two sites - one near Kimbolton, and another in Peterborough - here's what she thought In an age when so much socialising revolves around screens, there's something really refreshing about gathering around a table, picking up some board games and spending a few hours laughing with friends. Ready Steady Roll is the sort of place you could easily drive past without ever knowing it exists. Yet this award-winning board game café was exactly what we were looking for when we stumbled on it during a Google search while looking for a halfway meeting place that offered more than the usual coffee shop or pub catch-up. As life gets busier, maintaining friendships when living in different towns many miles apart can become surprisingly difficult – so finding somewhere worth travelling to is a challenge. Thankfully, Ready Steady Roll offered the perfect solution, with an afternoon packed with laughter, nostalgia and friendly competition. The venue boasts an extensive games library with options ranging from light-hearted family favourites to deeper strategy games. Our afternoon began in unfamiliar territory with Shoot for the Stars, a “general knowledge” game with questions like how many beans in a can of Heinz. We then opted for a healthy dose of nostalgia, transporting back to childhood with the classics Frustration and Operation, before picking up Doodle Rush, a quick-fire drawing game. Whether you're a seasoned gamer or someone whose experience begins and ends with Ludo and Monopoly, there's something to tempt everyone of all ages with every genre imaginable neatly packed on well organised shelves – most of which we'd never heard of before. Board games are only half the story. The café serves a great selection of food and drinks, and we happily worked our way through impressive coffee, chips, sausage rolls and cakes during our four-hour visit. The table service meant we could stay immersed in the games while the food and drinks arrived at our table, helping create an unhurried atmosphere. Perhaps what stood out most was the welcome. The venue feels warm, cosy and genuinely inviting, somewhere that encourages you to settle in and stay awhile. It was a joy to escape to. There is also a strong community feel. Alongside regular daytime gaming, the venue hosts board-game evenings where people can come along, meet fellow enthusiasts and join games with others. For anyone looking to expand their social circle or simply find opponents for a favourite game, it's a lovely idea. What makes Ready Steady Roll special is that it offers something increasingly rare: a chance to slow down. No notifications, no scrolling, no rush. Just good company, good food, plenty of laughter and hundreds of games waiting to be explored. For three friends from across the region, Ready Steady Roll turned an ordinary catch-up into a memorable day out, leaving us already planning our next visit. Need to Know Where: Studio 5, Ivy Lodge, Rushden Road, Sharnbrook, MK44 1ND. Cost: £4 for adults and £3 for children for a two-hour session. Weekday term-time sessions are £2. Opening times: check the Ready Steady Roll website and social media channels for current opening hours.

metadata.title: Council 'does not intend to progress' plans to build on Hunts car parks
metadata.contentSnippet: Huntingdonshire District Council "does not intend to progress" Capital & Centric plans to build on car parks in St Neots, St Ives and Huntingdon.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Council 'does not intend to progress' plans to build on Hunts car parks
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. The council "does not intend to progress" plans to build housing developments on three Huntingdonshire car parks after 90% of residents opposed the scheme. Plans by developer Capital & Centric and Huntingdonshire District Council (HDC) to build homes on three large car parks in St Neots, Huntingdon and St Ives sparked fury among residents in August. The plans for the St Neots Tebbutts Road car park include two five-storey buildings, up to 83 homes and units for independent businesses. The newly released Gateway 1 report reveals that out of resident responses, 91.2% opposed the plans in St Ives, 89.8% opposed the plans in St Neots and 87% opposed the plans in Huntingdon. After the completion of the Gateway 1 stage, which included public engagement, technical surveys, and concept designs, the council "does not intend to progress to Gateway 2 with Capital and Centric on the current schemes", the report reveals. Residents turned out in force to share their views about the plans to develop Tebbutts Road (Image: Emily Stevens) In a statement, the council said: "The scale and consistency of public opposition is focused on the fundamental choice of sites rather than design detail; unresolved strategic parking and accessibility issues remain; and the economic case does not outweigh the identified concern regarding parking function and public feedback." The main concern raised was the impact of redeveloping central surface car parks on the vitality and accessibility of town centres. The council’s decision follows pre-application advice from the planning authority, which stressed the need for a comprehensive parking strategy before any redevelopment could be considered. Officers concluded that the evidence did not provide a strong enough case to justify further investment in the next stage of the project. An independent review of the Capital & Centric commission will continue, and the technical work completed to date will remain available for future use. The full report will be discussed at an extraordinary meeting of HDC at 7pm on Tuesday, November 24.

metadata.title: Councillors vote to approve 600-home plan for St Neots
metadata.contentSnippet: Huntingdonshire District Councillors have voted to approve a a plan for up to 600 new homes on land at Priory Hill in St Neots.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Councillors vote to approve 600-home plan for St Neots
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Councillors have voted to approve a a plan for up to 600 new homes in St Neots. The outline application by Bloor Homes for land at Priory Hill, north of St Neots would create a new neighbourhood between Priory Hill Road, Huntingdon Road, the River Great Ouse, and the East Coast Main Line. The site sits close to Priory Park (Image: Newsquest) St Neots Town Council and Little Paxton Parish Council have both lodged objections to the scheme. The town council said it is concerned that "the development would place additional pressure on local services and infrastructure, particularly secondary school provision" and raised additional concerns over loss of agricultural land, flood risk and drainage. Additionally, HDC has received a total of 92 objections from residents. At a meeting of Huntingdonshire District Council's Development Management Committee on November 16, councillors voted to approve the application in line with planning officer recommendations. Councillors debated the plan for more than two hours, initially rejecting the motion to approve the plan. After more debate, a motion to refuse the plans was proposed by Cllr Alan Hunt and seconded by Cllr Stephen Ferguson. The result was a tie of six votes for and six against, so Chair Cllr Warren Smith had the casting vote and rejected the motion to refuse. Cllr Tom Sanderson put forward a proposal to approve the application, which resulted in another tie of five votes for, five against and two abstentions. Cllr Warren Smith again had the casting vote and the motion to approve the plans was passed. The scheme seeks permission for up to 600 homes, with 40 per cent designated as affordable housing. Alongside the housing, the plans include a community hub, mobility hub, public open space, allotments, walking and cycling routes, landscaping, and associated infrastructure. There would also be changes to nearby road speed limits and junctions, along with the removal of a double-mini roundabout at Priory Hill.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: National Grid has reassured households that there is no national power outage expected on Thursday, November 19, following claims circulating on social media. The organisation issued a statement after becoming aware of a post claiming there would be a National Grid outage on the date. National Grid said: “We’re aware of a false social media post claiming there will be a National Grid outage on Thursday, November 19 2026. “There is no outage expected. Please disregard the post and report misinformation to social media platforms. “Check our official channels for accurate information.” The warning comes amid a number of unrelated rumours about major blackouts circulating online during November. Other claims suggesting a widespread blackout would take place on November 17 have also circulated internationally, with fact-checking reports finding no evidence of a planned worldwide power cut. The November 19 claim also coincides with the highly anticipated release date of Grand Theft Auto VI, although there is no verified evidence establishing that the game is the source of the outage rumour. National Grid is encouraging people who encounter the false claim to report it to the relevant social media platform and rely on its official channels for accurate information.

metadata.title: Former timber mill to be demolished for homes despite flooding and traffic fears
metadata.contentSnippet: A former saw mill on Histon Road in Cottenham will be demolished to make way for affordable homes despite fears from residents over increased traffic.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Former timber mill to be demolished for homes despite flooding and traffic fears
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A former village saw mill will be demolished to make way for affordable homes despite fears from residents over increased traffic. South Cambridgeshire District Council’s planning committee approved the proposal for 34 affordable homes at the former timber mill on Histon Road in Cottenham. Though the site lies on the green belt, planning officers recommended the scheme for approval as it was “proportionate to Cottenham village”. Luke Webb, planning director at the applicant Living Space Housing, said it would be a “positive use of a current brownfield site” and they aimed to start building as “early as possible in 2027”. Cottenham Parish Council objected to the plans as they feared they would overwhelm local infrastructure, noting that 34 homes had already been approved nearby. Jo Brook said the parish council recognises the need for affordable housing but this “does not automatically make every site suitable for development.”. She said families would face a half hour walk to primary school or nursery which would encourage them to drive. She said: “For families, that’s a considerable journey and many will inevitably choose to drive. “This is particularly concerning when the school is already exploring a scheme to close Lambs Lane at drop-off and collection times because of existing parking and congestion problems.” Ms Brook added that it is “well documented” that the surrounding properties on Histon Road “flood regularly”. Cllr Heather Williams, of The Mordens, said she “can completely understand” their concerns about the cumulative impact, but it has to be weighed against housing need. The Conservative councillor said: “We can see from the officer’s report that there is need and, to be quite frank, there is going to be an increasing need for a long time. “I think there is a danger with all these applications that you don’t end up actually putting all the social housing together and I would say that this is probably its limit for that.” Cllr Dr Martin Cahn, of Histon and Impington, said that Cottenham is “a very unusual village” as it is “an extremely long village”. The Lib Dem councillor said: “Where is the centre? It’s strung along a long distance – any development in Cottenham is going to be too far from some of the facilities. “I don’t see that as a reason to refuse it and it will be a valuable addition to our social housing, which is a high priority in our district.” Cllr Anna Bradnam, chair of the committee, said there was a “substantial justification” for housing in the area and added that the proposal now has a “very comprehensive surface water drainage scheme”. The Lib Dem councillor said: “It’s possible that this will actually make it less likely that those properties on Histon Road flood – let us hope so.” The plans were approved unanimously by the planning committee.
