metadata.title: Met Office forecasts snow for the UK in coming days - where 9cm per hour could fall
metadata.contentSnippet: The Met Office has forecast snow from Monday (November 16), with falls expected in Scotland, Wales, and northern England - see exactly where.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Met Office forecasts snow for the UK in coming days - where 9cm per hour could fall
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Snow has been forecast across parts of the UK early next week, with some areas set for falls of up to 9cm per hour. The Met Office has forecast "wintry showers", along with hill snow, and strong coastal winds between Monday (November 16) and Wednesday (November 18). The forecast reads: "Sunny for most on Monday, but wintry showers over northeast Scotland and rain for the southwest later. "From Tuesday, rain, hill snow in the north, showers, and strong coastal winds." Are you hoping for some snow?☃️ Colder air will make a return next week, but this time it will be joined by more unsettled weather. This means there is likely to be some snow in places. How much and where is still uncertain but there is the potential for some disruption due to snow and ice. — Met Office (@metoffice) November 13, 2026 Snow is expected to fall in the Scottish Highlands as early as Sunday (November 14), according to WX Charts weather maps. By late Monday, snow could move into South Wales around Merthyr Tydfil before spreading north overnight toward Newtown and Welshpool. Early Tuesday (November 17) could see further snowfall in parts of Yorkshire, Cumbria, and southern Scotland, reaching as far as Glasgow and Stirling. The most widespread snowfall across the UK is expected early on Tuesday (November 17). (Image: WX Charts) WX charts shows snow lingering around small areas of Scotland until the following Wednesday (November 25). This is likely to be the only snow the UK sees for the rest of November, according to the Met Office. The Met Office’s long-range forecast (for November 19 to 28) suggests a mix of rain and showers, particularly in the south and west, with drier, colder spells in between. The forecast reads: "A changeable pattern is likely to continue, with areas of rain or showers affecting parts of the UK, particularly across the south and west. "These will be interspersed with drier, colder interludes as shorter-lived ridges of high pressure develop. "Weather patterns may become slower evolving during the latter stages of November, leading to some uncertainty over how much progress Atlantic frontal systems will make into the UK. "Nonetheless, further rain or showers are likely at times, with the potential for some periods of strong winds. "Incursions of milder air are likely towards the south, although it could remain on the cold side overall further north, where there is potential for overnight frosts and occasional wintry precipitation, particularly over higher ground." Cold weather health alerts have also been issued for large parts of the UK. During winter, lots of illnesses like flu, and COVID-19 spread easily. If you're unwell, there are actions you can take to reduce the risk of spreading infections to others. 🤒 https://t.co/8hdhDCK9wS — UK Health Security Agency (@UKHSA) November 13, 2026 The warnings are expected to affect the North West, West Midlands, and Yorkshire and the Humber from 9pm on Sunday (November 15) until 9am on Thursday (November 19). The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said the alerts mean the weather is likely to have minor impacts on health and social care services, including an increased use of healthcare services and a greater risk to life to vulnerable people. Paul Coleman, consultant in public health at the UKHSA, said: "This is the latest Cold-Health Alert of the season, and we can expect more as we move further into winter. "Cold weather can have a serious impact on the health of some people, including those aged 65 and over and those with pre-existing health conditions, so it is vital to check in on friends, family and neighbours who are most vulnerable." Mr Coleman said people should try to keep the rooms they use most heated and dress warmly during colder spells. Is there snow forecast near you this week? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: Aldi admits 'big mistake' as it brings back popular feature after shopper complaints
metadata.contentSnippet: Aldi has admitted making “a big mistake” which left customers disappointed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Aldi admits 'big mistake' as it brings back popular feature after shopper complaints
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Aldi has admitted making “a big mistake” which left customers disappointed, but it has now found a solution. Sharing the announcement on Instagram, the supermarket told customers that it would be changing its packaging for tortilla wraps. Known for its online humour, the team behind Aldi's social media accounts said it was making “a real” statement “because we as a supermarket made a big mistake”. The packaging for tortilla wraps wasn’t resealable to begin with, but then Aldi made the pack resealable to help with freshness and ease of storage. In 2025, it decided to remove the resealable tabs on the packets, but now they’re back, much to customers’ delight. Aldi added: “Back in 2025 we made a choice, like many others have done, to remove the sticky resealable tabs on our tortilla wraps. “You lot had lots of thoughts. “Apparently you really love a peel and reseal. “We don’t blame you. “It is a peak wrap storage method. “Cut a long story short (we’re on a word count), we made some calls. “The resealable packs are coming back! “You’ll find them in stores right now so you best thank us by buying a pack or four. “The kids want fajitas for tea every night (it’s us, we’re the kids).” The U-turn has delighted Aldi shoppers, with one saying: “This is big news”. Another said: “This has made my day!!” This person commented: “Thank god for that”. Someone else said: “I’m actually THRILLED about this!! “Thank goodness!”. The change saw other customers suggest the supermarket bring back some of their favourite items. This person said: “Can you also bring back the peanut butter balls cereal?!” Another commented: “Bring back the Almond and hazelnut florentines pleeeeeease!!!!” Recommended reading: Someone else said: “Yes now when are you gna bring back your carbonara in a jar?? “It’s been YEAAAARSSSS”. Which Aldi product do you wish would return to shelves? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: Mayor tours innovative AMFRESH and Encocam businesses in Alconbury Weald
metadata.contentSnippet: Two Alconbury Weald businesses making waves in manufacturing and fresh produce recently welcomed a visit from the mayor.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Mayor tours innovative AMFRESH and Encocam businesses in Alconbury Weald
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two businesses making waves in manufacturing and fresh produce recently welcomed a visit from the mayor. Paul Bristow, mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, toured AMFRESH and Encocam at Alconbury Weald in Huntingdonshire to see first-hand how these companies are contributing to the region’s economy through innovation and industry partnerships. AMFRESH, a family-owned Spanish company with a presence in Peterborough, operates a packhouse and laboratory focused on citrus fruits, grapes, juices and other fresh produce. Matvii Smirnov, innovation director at AMFRESH, said: "We were delighted to welcome Paul Bristow and his team to our OMEGA Innovation Centre and to see the strong interest from the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority in our efforts to deliver the highest quality and nutritional value to consumers." The company recently opened its OMEGA centre, which is dedicated to advancing fruit biochemistry and packing technology. Mr Bristow praised the company’s approach. He said: "It's great to see such innovation happening in our agri-tech sector. "AMFRESH is working with local schools, training skilled young people and contributing towards our regional economy." Encocam, a globally recognised advanced manufacturing business, focusing on automotive safety technologies and advanced engineering, was the mayor’s second stop. During his visit, Mr Bristow toured Encocam’s crash test dummy facility and discussed opportunities and challenges facing the automotive sector. Mayor Paul Bristow with James French at Encocam (Image: Combined Authority) Chris Hartley, HR manager at Encocam and a former apprentice, highlighted the company’s commitment to skills development. He said: "I continued my development with the support of some amazing workplace mentors and module tutors at Cambridge Regional College. "We see great potential in all our young people and recognise their importance to the future of our business. "That’s why we strive to give them the best support and training opportunities." Encocam has delivered more than 20 apprenticeship schemes over the past decade.

metadata.title: Russell Brand reportedly moved to Cambridgeshire prison
metadata.contentSnippet: Russell Brand has reportedly been moved to a category C prison in Cambridgeshire, HMP Littlehey near Huntingdon, according to The Sun on Sunday.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Russell Brand reportedly moved to Cambridgeshire prison
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Russell Brand has reportedly been moved to a category C prison in Cambridgeshire. The 51-year-old comedian was convicted of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others before being sentenced to 10 and a half years in prison on Monday, November 9. Brand was also cleared of two further rape charges and an allegation of attempted indecent assault, while police are investigating two further rape allegations. The Sun on Sunday reported that Brand was transferred from HMP Wandsworth in London to HMP Littlehey near Huntingdon on Friday, November 13. The move was reportedly prompted by safety concerns, while Brand was classed as a low escape risk. HMP Littlehey houses around 1,200 inmates and offers activities including yoga, choir, indoor bowls and an inter-wing football league. The prison houses inmates convicted of sexual offences. Brand is believed to be held in a single-person cell on E Wing, and has reportedly not yet interacted with other prisoners. He is expected to serve two-thirds of his sentence before being released on licence. He will also remain on the sex offenders’ register for life.

metadata.title: Cambs libraries not removing David Walliams books, council confirms
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire libraries will not be actively removing David Walliams’ books from their shelves, Cambridgeshire County Council has confirmed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs libraries not removing David Walliams books, council confirms
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire libraries will not be actively removing David Walliams’ books from their shelves, the council has confirmed. Cambridgeshire County Council said its libraries will not be taking action to withdraw the author’s titles after an ITV News and The Guardian investigation saw him accused of sexual misconduct this week. Mr Walliams, 55, known for titles such as The Boy in the Dress and Gangsta Granny, wrote more than 40 books, which generated a revenue of £100 million by 2019. He has been accused of inappropriate sexual behaviour with girls allegedly as young as 15. He has also been accused of inappropriate conduct and sexual harassment at his former publisher HarperCollins, and while working on Britain’s Got Talent. Mr Walliams has denied all allegations of misconduct. Cambridgeshire County Council confirmed that Cambridgeshire Libraries "will not be actively removing" his books. A council spokesperson said: “Cambridgeshire Libraries is part of Libraries Connected, the body which represents all Public Library Services in England. "Libraries Connected has issued the below statement, which is consistent with our own Stock Policy, and specifically addresses the writings of David Walliams." Libraries Connected, which represents public library services across England, said that while all books should be available unless illegal, stock is routinely refreshed based on demand. Libraries Connected said: "In this case, we understand that demand for Walliams’s books has fallen significantly in recent years. "We would therefore expect the number of copies in circulation to decline naturally as they are replaced by newer and more popular titles, particularly as he is now without a publisher." Decisions about whether to keep Mr Walliams' books in Cambridgeshire schools will be made by governing bodies or trustee boards, the council confirmed. The council added that should the Department for Education issue any guidance, this would be shared with schools.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A body has been recovered from a river during the search for a missing man from Cambridgeshire Graeme Usher, 69, was last seen at around 8pm on Thursday, November 5, in March. He left his home in a silver Ford Focus. Cambridgeshire Police confirmed today (November 15) that officers recovered a body from the river last night, on November 14. His family have been informed of the development, but no formal identification has yet been carried out.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Aldi to cut vegetable prices to just 8p each for limited time before Christmas
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Aldi has confirmed that it will be reducing the price of some of its vegetables to just 8p before Christmas. The supermarket chain has reduced the price of its vegetables during the festive season in recent years, allowing customers to cut the cost of their Christmas dinner and this year the offer returns. metadata.title: Microsoft issues important update for all users following global outage
metadata.contentSnippet: Microsoft has issued an update, telling its customers that it has now fully restored its services after the global outage that started on Thursday this week.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Microsoft issues important update for all users following global outage
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Microsoft has fully restored services following a major global IT outage. The disruption affected police forces, the NHS, businesses, courts, and schools. The US-based company confirmed this morning (November 14) that services were fully restored for all remaining affected customers. In a statement on its Microsoft 365 status page, the company said: "We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions. We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services. This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions. Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration. We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete. — Microsoft (@Microsoft) November 13, 2026 "Further updates can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center." The outage, which began around 6pm GMT on Thursday, November 12, disrupted email, messaging, and other Microsoft 365 services. The UK Government and others worldwide were forced to activate contingency plans. Microsoft said on Friday the disruption was due to a "technical issue not related to cyber or AI agents." Baroness Lloyd of Effra, the UK Government’s cyber minister, said the problem mainly affected back-office functions. Baroness Lloyd said there had been "limited reports of impact on frontline service delivery" and the incident had been "inconvenient and disruptive". She confirmed she had spoken with Microsoft UK chief executive Darren Hardman about the outage. Monitoring website Downdetector first showed a spike in users reporting problems with Microsoft Teams in the UK at about 6.15pm on Thursday. It recorded a surge in complaints, with more than 130,000 users in the US reporting problems with Outlook at its peak on Thursday evening. Millions of its customers were unable to send and receive emails through Outlook, while Microsoft’s Copilot AI assistant, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services were also affected for many. Other AI chat platforms, including OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude, were disrupted. Police forces in England and Wales said on Friday that they could not receive crime reports online. NHS England said staff had switched to "long-standing measures" to manage the outage, including the use of paper records. Rail passengers were unable to access e-tickets for their journeys as they couldn't open the emails in their Outlook inboxes. National Rail warned travellers to use alternative methods to access their tickets. A spokesman said: "We’re aware of the ongoing Microsoft global outage, which may be affecting customers’ ability to access their train tickets via their email inbox. "If you’re unable to locate or access your tickets through your email due to this issue, you may still be able to access your tickets by visiting the website or app where you purchased your tickets from and logging into your account. ‼️We’re aware of the ongoing Microsoft global outage, which may be affecting customers’ ability to access their train tickets via their email inbox. 🔗Latest Information and advice can be found here: https://t.co/pYa714hR8k — National Rail (@nationalrailenq) November 13, 2026 "We recommend doing this before you travel to ensure you have your tickets readily available for your journey. "This may not be possible if you checked out as a guest – please contact your ticket retailer directly if you are unable to access your tickets. "If you are still unable to access your ticket, please contact a member of onboard staff or station staff for advice." Other rail operators, including Southeastern, Chiltern Railways and London North Eastern Railway (LNER), reported similar problems with emailed tickets. Did the global Microsoft 365 outage affect you this week? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: Rare fish 'considered locally extinct' found in Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: A critically endangered species of fish has been discovered in a Cambridgeshire waterway, despite being thought to be extinct locally.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Rare fish 'considered locally extinct' found in Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A rare fish thought to be extinct locally has been discovered in Cambridgeshire. The sturgeon, weighing 15lb, was found on the banks of the Twenty Foot Drain last week, the Environment Agency said. According to the Zoological Society of London, the UK is home to two native species of the fish. The Atlantic and European sturgeon can both reach up to five metres long and can live for more than 60 years. They are among the most critically endangered group of animals on the International Union for Conservation of Nature's Red List. The Environment Agency said it hadn't been made aware of any catch reports in the drains or surrounding rivers. "We have absolutely no idea what the story with this one is," a spokesperson said. They added: "Native sturgeon are considered locally extinct in our patch, although historically there have been reports from the River Great Ouse. "Reports exist of a 130lb sturgeon being caught in Huntingdon way back in 1754. "There have been introductions of the species in France in recent years with some of these fish migrating across the channel and being caught in UK waters." It is illegal to keep sturgeon in fisheries in England due to the risk of hybridisation with the few remaining native European sturgeon in the UK's waterways. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.contentSnippet: A man is fighting for his life in hospital after a robbery at Lala Jewellers in Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man is fighting for his life in hospital after a robbery at a jewellery shop in Cambridgeshire. Emergency services were called to Lala Jewellers, in Gladstone Street, Peterborough, at around 11.50am on Saturday (November 14). It follows reports six men entered the store, including two who were wearing white, traditional Pakistani clothing. Two employees behind the counter were assaulted and shelves were emptied, before the men fled in separate vehicles. One employee, a 50-year-old man, was seriously injured and rushed to hospital, where he remains in a life threatening condition. The other employee, a 30-year-old man, suffered minor injuries. Detective Inspector Tracy Sawyer said: "This is a very concerning incident which has left one man seriously injured and we are carrying out extensive enquiries to identify those responsible. "We would like to hear from anyone who was in the Gladstone Street area at around the time of the robbery and saw anything suspicious either before or after the incident. "We would also urge anyone with CCTV, doorbell or dashcam footage from the area which may have captured something relevant to please get in touch." Those with information should contact police online or via 101 quoting reference 35/88602/26. Information can also be reported anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555111. metadata.title: £200,000 funding secures Trusted Adult Scheme for young people until 2028
metadata.contentSnippet: A youth scheme is helping young people in Cambridge and Peterborough find their path and reach their potential.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: £200,000 funding secures Trusted Adult Scheme for young people until 2028
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A youth scheme is helping young people in Cambridge and Peterborough find their path and reach their potential. The Trusted Adult Scheme (TAS), funded by Police and Crime Commissioner, Darryl Preston, with support from Anglia Ruskin University (ARU), offers a safe space for 13 to 18-year-olds to explore new opportunities, build confidence, and develop life skills through weekly sessions. Darryl Preston, police and crime commissioner, said: "Funding projects like the Trusted Adult Scheme (TAS) delivers on many levels offering the group new and different experiences in supported environments. Young people can access mentoring, activities and safe spaces through the scheme. (Image: Trusted Adult Scheme) "Often young people need someone to talk to, to confide in and this trust is something which only grows when they feel safe, seen and heard within an inclusive environment." The programme, led by criminology lecturer Dr Paul Nelson, includes young people who are not in education, employment, or training (NEET), who may be exhibiting risky behaviours. Since its inception, the commissioner has committed more than £200,000 of Home Office grant funding to the scheme, securing its future until March 2028. Dr Nelson said: "By receiving further funding for two years we can provide art sessions, music studios to record in, gaming and street art sessions alongside outdoor activities like laser tag. The Trusted Adult Scheme supports young people across Cambridge and Peterborough (Image: Trusted Adult Scheme) "The 13 to 18-year-olds come to us needing support, guidance and encouragement – seeing them leave as matured individuals just can't be measured." Each week, the scheme offers activities such as street art, sports, gaming, creative arts and crafts, and one-to-one mentoring. Young people have shared positive feedback about their experiences. New funding will help the youth programme continue until 2028 (Image: Trusted Adult Scheme) One participant said: "TAS is the first place I’ve felt listened to. "It’s helped me stay out of trouble and focus on what I want to do next." Referrals to the scheme are made by partners in Education and Targeted Support at Cambridgeshire County Council.

UK food supplier used by Aldi collapses and closes with 662 jobs lost
metadata.contentSnippet: Kanes Foods - which supplied Aldi, Lidl, and Asda with salads, stir-fries, and sauces - has ceased trading after entering administration, with 662 jobs lost.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK food supplier used by Aldi collapses and closes with 662 jobs lost
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A major UK food supplier has collapsed into administration and ceased trading, resulting in the loss of more than 650 jobs. Kanes Foods, established in 1989, produced pre-packaged salads, stir-fry products and sauces (with a short shelf life) for major supermarkets, including: After 37 years in business, Kanes Foods has collapsed into administration. Timothy Andrew Higgins, Edward Williams and Helen Wheeler-Jones of PwC were appointed joint administrators on Monday (November 9). Following the appointment, Kanes Foods ceased "with immediate effect", and all 662 employees were made redundant. Joint administrator and director at PwC, Tim Higgins, said: "It is deeply regrettable that a long-established business with a strong reputation has been left with no option but to enter administration, and that so many hard-working employees have lost their jobs as a result. "We recognise how difficult a time this is for employees and their families and we will support those affected through the redundancy process." Kanes Foods had been under financial and operational strain for several years. In June 2025, a failure at its wastewater treatment plant led to approximately £2 million in one-off costs and higher ongoing operating expenses. Further disruption came in August 2026, when drought-related supply issues affected trading during the crucial summer season. The company also faced continued losses, negative cash flow and uncertainty over future demand. Directors explored options such as refinancing and securing new investment, but no viable solutions were found. A fast-track sale process began in mid-September 2026, but administrators were unable to secure a going concern sale in time. Administrators said they will support affected employees in making claims to the Redundancy Payments Service. It has been a tough year for the UK high street, with several retailers entering administration or liquidation and others announcing widespread store closures. Major high street brands Claire's and Quiz have been forced to close all their remaining stores after falling into administration. UK fashion retailer Leading Labels is also set to close its remaining 15 stores after falling into liquidation in May. Whitbread closed all its standalone branded restaurants across the UK last month, affecting five brands: However, Queensway Inns and Common Table Group have now taken over 110 of these former Whitbread sites, saving them from closure. Poundland has filed a notice to appoint administrators, putting the future of its 150 stores and 11,000 employees at risk. TG Jones and the British Heart Foundation will also be closing around 150 stores each across the UK. Wynsors World of Shoes is shutting 17 stores across the UK, with closing down sales already underway at several affected branches. UK entertainment retailer Zavvi has ceased trading after nearly 20 years, having collapsed into administration for a second time. Australian stationery retailer Typo is also set to pull out of the UK in 2027, closing all its stores and ending online trading. Other retailers have been forced to close stores this year, including: Several UK travel companies have ceased trading or entered administration in 2026, including: Wayfairer Travel Limited has also suspended all services "until further notice" as it looks to appoint an administrator. Meanwhile, four UK airlines have fallen into administration or liquidation: Meanwhile, UK delivery company Yodel was phased out completely in July after being acquired by InPost. Iconic fashion brand Nasty Gal has also shut down its website after being sold by Debenhams in a deal worth around £12 million (US$16 million). It hasn't all been bad news for the UK high street, with several major brands announcing new store openings for 2026, including Joules, B&M, Aldi, M&S, and Superdrug. Meanwhile, brands including Evans and Bodycare have returned to the UK high street this year after previously closing all their stores. Which store/business closure in 2026 has impacted you the most? The discount supermarket's Specially Selected range has been crowned Own Label Range of the Year at the Quality Food Awards (QFAs), with judges recognising its food quality across a wide range of products. Aldi also took home 17 medals in total – including three golds, eight silvers and six bronzes – putting it ahead of some of the UK's biggest grocery names. The results will be particularly welcome news for shoppers looking to buy premium food without paying the prices often associated with higher-end supermarket ranges. The Quality Food Awards are judged by a panel of industry experts, including chefs, food scientists and food writers. Products are assessed on factors including ingredients, taste, aroma, packaging and value for money. Aldi Specially Selected mince pies (Image: Aldi) Among Aldi's biggest winners were three products that secured gold medals in their respective categories. Its Specially Selected Premium Wagyu Denver Steaks, priced at £6.99 for 227g, won Best Beef, while the £3.69 Gastro Mac & Cheese took the Best Ready Meals title. The supermarket also won Best Smoked Fish for its Specially Selected Lightly Smoked Scottish Salmon Fillets, which cost £4.29 for 240g. Recommended reading: All three products are available in Aldi stores now. Other familiar products from the range also received recognition, with silver medals awarded to: Aldi's latest award follows another successful year at the Quality Food Awards. The retailer was named QFA Christmas Retailer of the Year in September, while its Specially Selected East Anglian Fresh Whole Goose, priced at £11.99 per kg, won Christmas Product of the Year. Aldi Specially Selected crisps (Image: Aldi) Julie Ashfield, Chief Commercial Officer at Aldi UK, said: "Our team of buyers and suppliers work hard all year to ensure our Specially Selected range is the best for both quality and price - and being named Own Label Range of the Year by the prestigious QFAs is fantastic recognition of that, and proof that shoppers don’t have to pay more to eat well. "We’re particularly delighted to retain the title for a second year running - it’s a wonderful way to round off a fantastic year."

metadata.title: Government confirms new State Pension rates – see how much pensioners will get
metadata.contentSnippet: Government confirms new State Pension rates – see how much pensioners will get, with the full new State Pension rising to £250.70 a week

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Government confirms new State Pension rates – see how much pensioners will get
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Pensioners are set to receive a higher weekly State Pension from April 2027 after the Government announced the new payment rates for the next financial year. The full new State Pension will increase to £250.70 a week, up from £241.30, while the full basic State Pension will rise to £192.10 a week from £184.90. The increases amount to an extra £9.40 and £7.20 a week respectively, giving eligible pensioners hundreds of pounds more over the course of a year. The new figures have been set out in a House of Commons Library briefing published on Wednesday, November 11, covering the benefit and pension rates announced for the 2027/28 financial year. Both the basic and new State Pension will rise by 3.9% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in average weekly earnings between May and July 2026. The increase is part of the Government's commitment to the State Pension triple lock, which means payments rise each year by the highest of inflation, average earnings growth or 2.5%. The full weekly rates will be: Over a full year, the increase works out at around £488.80 for someone receiving the full new State Pension and £374.40 for someone receiving the full basic State Pension. The new State Pension applies to people who reached State Pension age on or after April 6, 2016. The basic State Pension is the core payment under the old State Pension system, for people who reached State Pension age before that date. The figures are the full weekly rates. The amount an individual receives will depend on their National Insurance record and whether they qualify for the full entitlement. Recommended reading: Pension Credit is also set to rise by 3.9% from April 2027, with the standard minimum guarantee increasing to: Pension Credit is a means-tested benefit designed to top up the income of people who have reached State Pension age and are on a lower income. It can also provide access to other support, including help with housing costs and some health-related expenses.

metadata.title: Millions could be affected by DWP benefits decision – full limits revealed
metadata.contentSnippet: The DWP plans to freeze the Benefit Cap for 2027/28. See the proposed weekly, monthly and annual limits for couples and single households.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Millions could be affected by DWP benefits decision – full limits revealed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The DWP has revealed they plan to freeze the maximum amount Brits can claim in benefits from next year. The Department for Work and Pensions updated their website on Wednesday, November 11, to outline proposed benefits rates for the 2027-28 tax year. Benefits caps are used by the government to limit the total amount of money claimants can receive and it applies to most people over 16 and below State Pensions age. -Widowed Parent’s Allowance (or Widowed Mother’s Allowance or Widow’s Pension if you started getting it before 9 April 2001) The current annual maximum for couples (with or without children) or single claimants with a child of qualifying age is £22,020 or £25,323 for those in Greater London. The annual maximum for single adults households this tax year, which ends in April, is £14,753 or £16,967 in Greater London. This is proposed to be frozen for the 2027-28 tax year, meaning Brits won't be able to claim more than this amount between April 2027 and 2028. The monthly equivalent is also planned to be frozen at £1,835 and £2,110.25 (Greater London) for couples, with or without children, or single claimants with a child of qualifying age. Single households without children face the same freeze, with the maximum remaining at £1,229.42 and £1,413.92 in Greater London. Weekly equivalents are planned to remain at £423.46 and £486.98 (Greater London) for couples, with or without children, or single claimants with a qualifying-age. The weekly maximum for single households is planned to remain at £283.71 or £326.29 (Greater London). This is despite the Office for National Statistics' most recent inflation rate being recorded at 3.6% in September and many economists forecasting that this is expected to rise next year. The government explains that the cap may not start for nine months if someone is claiming Universal Credit but this depends on their earnings. Recommended reading: Brits are not affected by the benefits cap if they or their partner get Universal Credit because of a disability that 'stops them from working' or get it because they care for someone with a disability. They're also exempt if they get Universal Credit and they or their partner earn £881 or more a month combined, after tax and National Insurance contributions.

metadata.title: 2 Tesco products recalled as shoppers warned 'do not eat' them
metadata.contentSnippet: Two pie products sold at Tesco have been recalled due to incorrect labelling, posing a health risk to some shoppers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 2 Tesco products recalled as shoppers warned 'do not eat' them
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two pie products sold at Tesco have been recalled due to the packaging being labelled incorrectly. The affected items are the Tesco Steak and Guinness Pie (200g) and the Tesco 6 Steak and Guinness Mini Pies (198g). These items contain milk but their packaging does not declare it, posing a possible risk to anyone who is allergic to milk or has an intolerance to milk or milk constituents. All use-by dates of both products up to and including November 23, 2026 are being recalled. Friday 13 November - Tesco recalls various Tesco Steak and Guinness Pie products because of undeclared milk https://t.co/rbMS6CajIu #FoodAllergy https://t.co/iRhHJzurDg https://t.co/IUIXhKJIBY — Food Standards Agency (@foodgov) November 13, 2026 The Food Standards Agency (FSA) has warned customers: “If you have bought any of the above products and have an allergy or intolerance to milk or milk constituents, do not eat them.” Instead, customers must return them to the Tesco store where they bought them so they can get a full refund. No receipt is needed to receive the refund and if you need more information, you can use Tesco’s contact page to get in touch. Tesco reassured customers that no other products are affected by this recall and apologised for any inconvenience to customers. The FSA explains what an allergy alert is and why they are issued: “Sometimes there will be a problem with a food product that means it should not be sold. “Then it might be 'withdrawn' (taken off the shelves) or 'recalled' (when customers are asked to return the product). Recommended reading: “Sometimes foods have to be withdrawn or recalled if there is a risk to consumers because the allergy labelling is missing or incorrect or if there is any other food allergy risk. “When there is a food allergy risk, the FSA will issue an Allergy Alert.” Do you shop at Tesco? metadata.title: UK airline ordered into compulsory liquidation 7 years after being founded
metadata.contentSnippet: The virtual UK airline Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation seven years after it was founded in 2019

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK airline ordered into compulsory liquidation 7 years after being founded
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation following a winding-up petition. The UK startup, which planned to use a fleet of Airbus A380 planes, was formally ordered to wind up by the Insolvency and Companies Court on Wednesday, November 4. The winding-up petition was originally filed in May, with several hearings held in the following months, including the most recent in October. The Gazette published the notice on Thursday, November 12, confirming the order. Former company directors Tom Stokely and Prashant Uttamchandani joined the case as supporting creditors and were represented by the law firm Katten Muchin Rosenman. With the order now in place, an officer of the court—known as the official receiver—has taken control of winding up the company. Government guidelines state that once a winding-up order is issued, the company’s bank accounts are typically frozen and its assets sold off to repay creditors. Companies have the right to apply for cancellation of a winding-up order within five working days if they believe the action is unwarranted. As of the latest update, Global Airlines is still listed as active on Companies House, though its most recent accounts are overdue. Global Airlines has been contacted by Newsquest for comment. Global Airlines Limited operated as a virtual airline with ambitions to operate a fleet of four Airbus A380 aircraft. The company, which was founded in 2019, acquired its only aircraft in May 2023, and claimed to be the first new A380 owner in eight years. Its maiden flight, operated under a damp lease from Hi Fly Malta, flew from Glasgow to New York-JFK on May 15, 2025. After completing just four transatlantic flights, the aircraft was placed into long-term storage in Tarbes, France, on July 16, 2025, with no known return-to-service date. Discussing its vision for the company, Global Airlines shared: "We want to deliver the Best Way to Fly. "And whether flying Global Traveller, Business or First, we believe we will. "Flying to a variety of destinations all over the world, we will breathe new life into onboard product and service, working with some amazing brands, delivering genuine value for money for our passengers. "And by embracing the latest technology and deploying it across every touch point, we can work smarter and deliver a Global experience that is unique to you." metadata.title: DWP disability benefit increase from 2027 for people who need care or mobility help
metadata.contentSnippet: The DWP has confirmed new Universal Credit rates from April 2027, with payments rising for people who need care or help with mobility

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP disability benefit increase from 2027 for people who need care or mobility help
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The DWP revealed that a million Brits could receive more Disability Living Allowance money from April next year. The Department for Work and Pensions updated their website on November 11 with proposals to increase the weekly payments. The current rates only cover the tax year between April 6 2026 and April 5 2027 so from April 6 next year new rates will apply. These increases are labelled as 'provisional' but the Government website's update history shows the previous provisional figures reflected the final figures to the penny. Disability Living Allowance, which helps cover the costs of extra personal care or mobility, has two components - care and mobility. Both of these are split from highest to lowest rates of payment depending on how severe the need for support is. People are eligible for the care component if they need help with things like washing, eating, cooking, communicating needs, dressing or using the toilet. They may also need supervision to 'avoid putting yourself or others in danger' or to have dialysis. The highest rate is paid to those who need 'help or supervision throughout both day and night, or if a medical professional has said they're nearing the end of their life'. This payment is proposed to rise from the £114.60 per week being paid during the current tax year to £118.60 per week for the 2027-28 tax year. The middle rate is described as being suitable for those who need 'frequent help or constant supervision during the day, supervision at night or someone to help you while on dialysis'. The lowest rate is for those who 'need help for some of the day or with preparing cooked meals' and this rate is proposed to increase from £30.30 per week to £31.35. The mobility component is for people who either cannot walk, can only walk 'short distances without severe discomfort' or who could become 'very ill if they try to walk'. People may also get this if they have no feet or legs, are 100% blind or you were between ages 3-64 on April 11 2011 and have been certified as 'severely sight impaired'. Recommended reading: Other criteria include those at least 80% deaf, those who need someone with them when outdoors or those who are 'severely mentally impaired' with behavioural problems. The lower rate of payment is for those who need 'guidance or supervision outdoors' and this would rise from £30.30 per week to £31.35 in the 2027-28 tax year. The higher rate is for those who have 'any other, more severe, walking difficulty' than covered in the lower rate and this would increase from £80 to £82.80 under the proposed new rates. Payments are usually sent directly to claimants bank accounts every four weeks and if their circumstances change they are told to contact the Disability Service Centre.

metadata.title: MoneySavingExpert warns Virgin customers to check for 'sneaky' paid add-on
metadata.contentSnippet: MoneySavingExpert says Virgin Experience Days shoppers should check for a £9.99 annual membership they may not have intended to buy.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: MoneySavingExpert warns Virgin customers to check for 'sneaky' paid add-on
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Virgin Experience Days shoppers are being urged to check whether they were signed up to a paid membership without realising. MoneySavingExpert said its team found the £9.99-a-year Memory Makers+ subscription was being added to orders through a pre-ticked box at checkout. The consumer website said it spotted the issue when it visited the company's website on October 30 and reported it to the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA). MoneySavingExpert said Virgin Experience Days changed its website after the issue was raised, so the membership box was no longer selected by default. The membership offers discounts on purchases, free greeting cards and other benefits, and renews automatically each year. CMA guidance says businesses must obtain a customer's express consent before charging for optional extras. It says a pre-ticked box does not provide that consent when a customer must take action to avoid an extra charge. The regulator also says customers who did not expressly agree to an additional charge are legally entitled to claim a refund. MoneySavingExpert recommends searching email inboxes, including junk and spam folders, for an account activation message to check whether the membership was added. It advises customers who want to cancel or request a refund to contact memorymakers@virginexperiencedays.co.uk. A Virgin Experience Days spokesperson said: "Memory Makers+ remains a relatively new addition to our business, and we continually review and refine the programme based on performance data, customer feedback and regulatory developments." The company said most customers saved more than the cost of membership on their first purchase and that it received positive feedback about the scheme. The spokesperson added: "In the small number of cases where a customer wishes to cancel, we operate a seven day a week support operation where queries are handled within 24 hours."

People have taken to Downdetector to report the issues with over 3,000 reports being made at around 6pm last night (Thursday, November 12). The number of reports of Microsoft Outlook being down is currently rising again with 1,115 reports being made at 6am this morning (Friday, November 13). 29% of people have reported issues with logging in to Outlook while 26% have said they are struggling to receive messages and 23% are having issues with the app. We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. Microsoft said: “We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. “While we’re working to mitigate impact, we’ve confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region, more information will be provided in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors. “We're providing more information under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as https://status.cloud.microsoft.” As well as Outlook, Microsoft users are facing issues with several other apps including Microsoft 365 with over 600 people reporting issues this morning. Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice-president, has said the outages do not appear to be because of a cyber attack. Microsoft said: “We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed that change is not taking as expected." Downdetector is a website that allows users of popular services like Instagram, Facebook, and Virgin Media to share if they are having trouble with the services. Describing itself on its website, Downdetector is “where people go when services don’t work.” The site will also collect information about any service problems from social media and other factors on the web. metadata.title: M&S apologises after customer ate 'crispy moth' lurking in tortilla chips
metadata.contentSnippet: Suzanne Bailey says she found a moth in M&S tortilla crisps served with a family meal. M&S apologised and said it was investigating.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: M&S apologises after customer ate 'crispy moth' lurking in tortilla chips
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A woman says she found a moth in her M&S tortilla crisps after eating a third of the bag. Suzanne Bailey said she initially thought the object was a burnt tortilla when she served the crisps with a family meal. The 45-year-old said she then realised it was a moth, which she believed had been cooked with the crisps. M&S apologised, offered her a refund and said it was investigating with its supplier. The operations manager, from Liverpool, had bought a £1.25 bag of lightly salted tortilla crisps for a Mexican meal. She said her 13-year-old daughter Isabella had eaten one crisp and was sick after the discovery. Ms Bailey said: "I went to pick the burnt tortilla up and this is when I realised it was a moth. My little girl had a mouthful of food and threw up. "I was mortified as I had eaten approximately a third of the bag." She said she found what she believed were the moth's legs when she returned the crisps to the bag as evidence, leaving her concerned she might have eaten one. Ms Bailey added: "It's gross and absolutely disgusting. I'm not into bushtucker trials but it feels like I've done an M&S one. "We haven't been back to shop at M&S. I don't think I could eat tortilla chips again either." After the incident, she threw away the £10 meal and ordered a £20 takeaway to feed her family instead. After taking photographs, she said she submitted a complaint through the M&S website and called customer support. An M&S spokesperson said: "We take matters like this extremely seriously and are working closely with our supplier partner to investigate this fully." The spokesperson said: "We have been in touch with the customer directly to apologise for the inconvenience caused and offer a full refund."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Royal Mint Beatrix Potter 50p coin sells for more than 400 times face value on eBay
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Royal Mint Peter Rabbit 50p coin has sold on eBay for more than £200. The Royal Mint's Beatrix Potter collection began in 2016, marking 150 years since the author's birth. The first Peter Rabbit design showed a close-up of the character facing forward, complete with whiskers. Other 2016 designs featured Squirrel Nutkin, Mrs Tiggy-Winkle and Jemima Puddle-Duck. Four more designs arrived in 2017, featuring Tom Kitten, Benjamin Bunny, Jeremy Fisher and another Peter Rabbit. The 2018 Peter Rabbit and Flopsy Bunny designs each had a circulating mintage of 1.4 million. The Peter Rabbit editions from 2019 and 2020 were not put into general circulation. The seller described the coin as a 2016 Royal Mint Peter Rabbit 50p in silver proof, with a fineness of 0.925. The listing eventually sold for a total of £219.20, including a £9.03 buyer-protection fee. The Royal Mint lists the 2023 Atlantic Salmon 50p as the rarest circulating 50p, with a mintage of 200,000. Next on its list is the 2009 Kew Gardens 50p, with 210,000, followed by the 2011 Olympic football design, with 1,125,500. The date matters: the Royal Mint's table also records two million Atlantic Salmon 50p coins dated 2025. Other low-mintage circulating designs include the 2011 Olympic wrestling, judo and triathlon coins, alongside the 2018 Peter Rabbit and Flopsy Bunny 50ps. Mintage is the number of coins made, and a lower figure can make a design harder for collectors to find. A coin's condition, design, material and demand from collectors can also affect what someone is willing to pay. A genuine error can be of interest to collectors, but a seller's description alone is not independent verification. The Royal Mint advises buyers of second-hand coins to check for original packaging and, for proof editions, a certificate of authenticity. A specialist valuation can help an owner establish a coin's history and likely value.

metadata.title: PM gives flat owners new powers to challenge 'unfair' service charges
metadata.contentSnippet: Millions of leaseholders are set to gain new powers to challenge unfair service charges.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: PM gives flat owners new powers to challenge 'unfair' service charges
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of leaseholders are set to gain new powers to challenge unfair service charges. The government says more than three million leaseholders in England will benefit from the reforms, with the first changes planned for April 1, 2027. The measures are due to be introduced in stages through to November 2028, subject to parliamentary approval. From April 2027, leaseholders will be able to request information about their service charges, including details from previous years. Landlords will need a good reason to refuse to provide the information, according to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. Service charges are fees paid by leaseholders or tenants to cover the maintenance, repair and management of shared areas of a building. The ministry says the changes will give leaseholders a clearer picture of how their building is managed, maintained, repaired and insured. The first stage also includes stronger protection against having to pay a landlord's legal costs when challenging a charge. Landlords will need court or tribunal approval to pass on legal costs, while leaseholders will gain a right to recover their own legal expenses, the government says. Further measures are planned for November 1, 2027, when leaseholders will receive clearer information about charges, including details of building insurance and administration fees. There will also be stronger protections against excessive or unreasonable fees for arranging and managing insurance. Private landlords will have to use standardised service charge demand forms and provide financial accounts and annual reports from November 2027. Councils and housing associations will have until November 1, 2028 to introduce those forms, accounts and reports for their leaseholders. Kion Ahadi, chief executive of the Leasehold Advisory Service, said: "Service charges are the most common issue leaseholders contact us about. "We welcome these changes as an important step forward in helping people understand what they are paying for and challenge costs they believe are unfair. "Leaseholders need clear information about how their money is being spent and a fair opportunity to raise concerns. "Better access to that information and stronger protection from landlords’ legal bills will give them more confidence to hold their landlord to account."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of people claiming Universal Credit are set to receive a higher monthly payment next year, after the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) confirmed the new benefit rates. The Government has published its annual review of benefit payments, setting out how much claimants will receive from April 2027. Working-age and disability benefits will rise by 3.5%, with the new rates mainly coming into effect from April 12, 2027. Inflation-linked benefits and tax credits will rise by 3.5% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) rate of inflation for September 2026. Universal Credit standard allowances will receive an additional uplift as specified in the Universal Credit Act 2025. The basic and new State Pensions will be uprated by 3.9% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in the Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) index for May–July 2026. Universal Credit is currently paid to more than 8.4 million people across the UK. Due to the increase in line with CPI, and the additional uprating factor, in 2027/28 Universal Credit standard allowances will increase: Universal Credit is a means-tested benefit designed to help with living costs for people on a low income, out of work or unable to work. The number of people claiming it has increased as the DWP continues its managed migration programme, which is moving people from older benefits onto the newer system. Around 2.2 million Universal Credit claimants are in employment, while a significant number of others are not expected to work because of health conditions or caring responsibilities. Recommended reading: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden confirmed the increases in a statement to Parliament following the Budget. He said: “The new rates will apply in the tax year 2027-28 and will mainly come into effect from April 12 2027. “The other state pension and benefit rates covered by my statutory review will be increased by 3.5%, in line with the increase in the consumer prices index in the year to September 2026. “This includes most working-age benefits and other benefits for people below state pension age; benefits to help with additional needs arising from disability; statutory payments including statutory sick pay and statutory maternity pay; and additional state pension. The pension credit savings credit maximum amount will also increase by 3.5%.”

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation after the force received “a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences” against David Walliams. It comes after Walliams was named as the celebrity who tried to block the publication of his identity amid allegations of “inappropriate sexual activities” with girls and young women earlier this week. Multiple women have accused the comedian, 55, of sexually inappropriate behaviour and grooming, including when they were teenagers, according to an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News. Walliams denies all allegations against him. David Walliams has denied all allegatons made against him (Image: Aaron Chown/PA) The Met Police received a number of non-recent allegations against the former Britain’s Got Talent judge “in recent days”. In a statement on Friday (November 13), the Met said the complaints made are separate from those previously reported by ITV News and The Guardian. But it added those reports are being reviewed by officers “to establish whether there is any evidence of offences”. A joint investigation by ITV News and The Guardian alleges Walliams preyed on teenage girls and young women for sexual purposes. Multiple women accuse Walliams of “grooming” them as teenagers, while another described her alleged encounter with Walliams as “sexual assault”. Walliams is also accused of inappropriate conduct and sexual harassment at his former publisher HarperCollins, and while working on Britain’s Got Talent. 🚨 BREAKING: David Walliams is now being investigated by the Met Police over alleged "serious sexual offences" https://t.co/udBrHX7noC — Politics UK (@PolitlcsUK) November 13, 2026 Responding to the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams denied all allegations against him. He said: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with... I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. “And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did... “I am not a sexual predator... I have not broken the law... I am devastated that some of the women I met ten to twenty years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.” The former Britain’s Got Talent judge, known for appearing in comedy shows including Come Fly With Me and Little Britain alongside Matt Lucas, has sold more than 60 million copies of his children’s books globally. They include The Boy In The Dress, Fing, and Gangsta Granny, the latter of which was turned into a one-hour BBC special in 2013, followed by a sequel starring Sheridan Smith in 2022. Walliams’ book publisher HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025, after an investigation into allegations he had “harassed” young women, which Walliams strongly denied. Earlier this month, theme park Alton Towers permanently closed its World of David Walliams attraction, which featured rides inspired by the books. Walliams left Britain’s Got Talent in 2022 after he apologised for making “disrespectful comments” about auditioning contestants during filming breaks in January 2020 at the London Palladium. In 2023, Britain’s Got Talent producer Fremantle apologised and reached an “amicable resolution” with Walliams after the remarks he made while on the show were leaked.

metadata.title: Watch moment ATM thief found hiding in loft after nationwide crime spree
metadata.contentSnippet: A prolific thief who targeted cash machines across England and Wales, including Cambridgeshire, has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Watch moment ATM thief found hiding in loft after nationwide crime spree
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A prolific thief who targeted cash machines across England and Wales, including Cambridgeshire, has been jailed. Bogdan Gasparov, 40, used cash-trapping devices to steal more than £16,000 from at least 180 ATMs between May and October 2026. Police found him hiding in a loft crawl space during a raid on his Hardie Road home in Dagenham. Detective Sergeant Mike Simpson from ERSOU's Proactive Economic Crime Team (PECT) said: "This was not opportunistic offending. "Gasparov carried out a calculated campaign of theft, targeting cash machines across the country and repeatedly returning to steal money that belonged to unsuspecting customers. "What makes this case even more brazen is that Gasparov had previously been convicted for similar offences and deported from the UK, only to return illegally and resume the same criminal behaviour. "He clearly believed he could stay one step ahead of investigators. He couldn't. "Thanks to the determination of our officers and the strength of the evidence gathered, he has now been brought to justice once again." Gasparov targeted ATMs in Bury St Edmunds, Lowestoft and Sudbury in Suffolk, Great Yarmouth in Norfolk, Huntingdon and Peterborough in Cambridgeshire, and Harlow in Essex. He also struck near Nottingham, Oxford, Somerset, Bristol, Derby, Gloucester, Lincoln and the West Midlands, as well as in parts of Scotland and Wales. The scheme involved Gasparov posing as a legitimate customer, fitting homemade cash-trapping devices to ATMs, and leaving the area. When genuine customers attempted to withdraw money, the cash would become trapped in the device. Gasparov would then return later to retrieve the device and the stolen funds. CCTV from several locations repeatedly placed Gasparov at the scenes. A search of his vehicle uncovered clothing worn during the offences, homemade cash-trapping devices and tools to make them. Moldovan national Gasparov used several aliases and had previous convictions for similar crimes. He had re-entered the UK illegally after being deported. Within 24 hours of his arrest, he pleaded guilty at Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court to two counts of theft from an ATM, covering all the offences. He also admitted entering the UK in breach of a deportation order and possessing items for use in fraud. On November 9, Gasparov was jailed for three years and six months at Chelmsford Crown Court. He is expected to face another deportation hearing after his release.

metadata.title: £195,000 boost for Cambridgeshire victims amid early offender releases
metadata.contentSnippet: Extra support has been made available to victims of crime in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: £195,000 boost for Cambridgeshire victims amid early offender releases
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Extra support has been made available to victims of crime in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. The support is in response to concerns arising from the Early Release Scheme, which is seeing some offenders released from prison before their full sentence is served. Police and Crime Commissioner Darryl Preston has increased the capacity of the Victim and Witness Hub to ensure timely and comprehensive support for those affected. Darryl said: "I understand the anxiety such news could cause especially for victims of domestic violence. "That's why I am keen to raise awareness of the local offer of support available here in our county to ensure victims feel safe, informed and supported." The Victim and Witness Hub offers emotional and practical support, including referrals to home security services and enhanced emotional support programmes. Victim and Witness Care Co-ordinators can also reconnect individuals with specialist services they have previously used. Victims whose offenders are being released early will be notified and directed to support services in their area. For those worried about personal safety, the Bobby Scheme is available to provide home security assessments and install devices such as locks and video doorbells. Additional funding of £195,000 over two years has been allocated to increase support services. A national Offender Release Helpline, set up by Victim Support, is also available on 0808 168 9280. The helpline operates Monday to Friday from 9am to 5pm, excluding bank holidays. The Early Release Scheme, known as the Progression Model, applies to offenders with fixed-term sentences. It allows part of the sentence to be served in the community under supervision. All individuals released under the scheme are subject to licence conditions and a period of intensive supervision. Victims in Cambridgeshire seeking support can contact the Victim and Witness Hub on 0800 781 6818 or by emailing victimandwitnesshub@cambs.police.uk.

metadata.title: Support for pubs only ‘lip service’ after budget says landlady
metadata.contentSnippet: A Cambridge pub landlady has accused the government of only paying “lip service” to supporting hospitality following the latest budget.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Support for pubs only ‘lip service’ after budget says landlady
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridge pub landlady has accused the government of only paying “lip service” to supporting hospitality following the latest budget. Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey delivered the first budget of Andy Burnham’s government last month, with a number of changes for pubs. This includes raising the threshold for Small Business Rates Relief in England from £12k to £18k – meaning businesses with a rateable value below this will pay no business rates. But pub operators will also face higher wage bills with the national living wage for workers aged 21 and over increasing from £12.71 an hour to £13.21. Both changes will come into effect from April 2027 and alcohol duty will also increase in line with inflation from February 1. Hayley Pellegrini, who runs five pubs in the city with her husband Steve including The Portland Arms and The Alex, said she does not feel small businesses are getting the support they need. The 56-year-old said: “We work ridiculous hours and what we pay ourselves we worked out is probably below minimum wage. “But it’s a case of we just have to suck it up and get on with it. “I don’t feel like we are getting the support we need – they aren’t doing anything, they want to be seen as being pub goers and that but they aren’t doing anything. “It’s not just pubs, it’s small businesses in general – we have friends who have small businesses and they are struggling as well.” She said small businesses are discouraged from expanding as they will lose relief and face higher wage bills from increased national insurance contributions and the rise in wages. Ms Pellegrini said it was harder for them as a living-wage employer, but that they’re “fortunate” to be based in Cambridge with a steady stream of business from students and tourists. She said: “Why am I going to employ someone with no experience, when I could be paying someone with ten years of experience the same? I think we are losing the next generation of hospitality managers, in 10 or 15 years we might find we haven’t brought up the next generation of managers.” She said the government was being “narrowminded” by not considering a reduction in VAT – with more than 400,000 signing the VAT’s the Problem petition to cut it from 20 per cent to 10 per cent, in line with other countries in Europe like France, Spain and Italy. Ms Pellegrini said: “We were hoping that Andy Burnham was actually going to be the one who will do something, but now we think – ‘ah, here we go again’. “What worries me is our retirement – we’re so busy trying to keep the business afloat we aren’t actually able to put anything away for our retirement and we’re going to be a burden on the government. “I work long, unsociable, hours often seven days a week to keep this industry going – who am I doing this for? “The slice of the pie being taken off us is just getting bigger and bigger and bigger. “It seems to be targeted at small businesses while companies like Amazon pay a tiny proportion of tax. “Something needs to be redistributed – the rich are getting richer and the rest of us are working our butts off to try and make a living.”

your continued support. 🪔✨

SEND Coffee Morning

We would like to invite parents and
carers to our

on

Wednesday 21st October from
8:30am to 9:15am.

This is a wonderful opportunity to
meet with Miss Leach and other
families in an informal setting, ask
questions, share experiences, and
find out more about the support
available for children with additional
needs.

We are also pleased to welcome our
new

Link Educational Psychologist,

who will be attending the session to
introduce herself to parents and
carers and explain more about her
role within the school. Please follow
the link to confirm whether you will
be joining us for this event

SEND
Coffee Morning - Fill in form

We look forward to seeing you there
and hope you can join us for a coffee
and a chat. ☕

Parent Consultation
Appointments

We are pleased to let parents and
carers know that

Parent Consultation
appointments are now live and
available to book

.

These meetings provide a valuable
opportunity to discuss your child's
progress, celebrate their
achievements, and talk through any
areas where they may need
additional support. We strongly
encourage all families to book an
appointment with their child's class
teacher.

Appointments can be booked via

MCAS (My Child at School)

. Please
log in to the app and select your
preferred time slot as soon as
possible, as appointments are
allocated on a first-come, first-served
basis.

If you experience any difficulties
booking your appointment, please
contact the school office for
assistance.

Vancols school
photographs are now available to
view and order

using the

QR code on
your proof card.

If you have already scanned the QR
code and registered, you should
receive an automatic email
notification when your photographs
are ready to view.

If you have not yet registered, don't
worry. Simply scan the QR code on
your proof card and follow the
instructions provided to access your
photographs online.

If you have not received your proof
card, or it has been misplaced, please
contact the

Vancols Parent Line on
01206 273711.

Please note that if you
do not already have a Vancols
account, you will need to contact the

code required to access your images.

We hope you enjoy viewing this year's

Cost of Living Support Update

We would like to make families aware
that the

Cambridgeshire Holiday
Voucher Scheme has now ended.

While holiday vouchers are no longer
available, a range of support
continues to be offered for families
who may be experiencing financial
difficulties.

The

Crisis and Resilience Fund

has
replaced the Household Support
Fund and is available until

31 March
2029

. Eligible families may be able to

previously received holiday vouchers
may be prioritised where appropriate.

We also encourage eligible families to
explore the

Holiday Activities and
Food (HAF) Programme

, which

healthy meals and snacks for children

For further information about

Cambridgeshire County Council
website or contact the School Office,

families to additional sources of help.

We are pleased to let Year 4 parents
and carers know that

deposits are
now payable via the MCAS app

for
our exciting residential visit to

Grafham Water

Monday 28th June to Wednesday 30th
June 2027.

To

secure your child’s place, a non-
refundable deposit of £75

Once the deposit has been paid, the

remaining balance can be paid in
monthly instalments through MCAS.

We hope that offering the opportunity

We are very much looking forward to

, or a similar group, to

🐻💛

announcements.title: EEBSA-Environmental and Emotional Barriers to Scho
announcements.content:
EEBSA

-Environmental

and Emotional

Barriers to

School

Attendance

Environmental and Emotional
Barriers to School Attendance
(EEBSA) is a term used to describe a
child's difficulty attending or
engaging with school due to
emotional factors. Children may
display EEBSA in a variety of ways,
and recognising the early signs can
help ensure they receive the right
support (please see the image
provided by Cambridgeshire County
Council highlighting signs of
EEBSA).

If you have concerns that your child
may be showing signs of EEBSA,
please speak to your child's class
teacher or a member of the Senior
Leadership Team. By working
together, we can develop a shared
understanding of your child's
strengths and any barriers they may
be facing, with the aim of supporting
their wellbeing and helping them feel
happy and successful at school.

Miss Westwood

will be hosting an
informal

Coffee Afternoon on
Wednesday 18th November from
2:30pm to 3:00pm

. Parents and carers
are warmly invited to attend to find
out more about EEBSA, discuss any
concerns, and learn about the support
available.

We look forward to seeing you there.

announcements.title: Attendance Update: Termly Pizza Parties (TAPP) & Appointment Guidelines
announcements.content:
Attendance Update

Medical appointments

will continue
to be authorised only when
appointment confirmation is provided
to the school office.

Optician
appointments

will no longer be
authorised from September, as these
can usually be arranged outside
school hours.

We are also delighted to launch our

Termly Attendance Pizza Parties
(TAPP).

Pupils achieving

98%
attendance or above

each term will be
invited to a special pizza party during
the final week of term and will
receive a raffle ticket for the chance
to win a

£50 Amazon voucher.

At Warboys Primary Academy, we
know that good attendance plays a
vital role in children's academic
achievement, social development and
wellbeing. Thank you for your
continued support in helping your
child attend school regularly and
arrive on time, giving them the very
best opportunity to thrive.

Term-time leave

We appreciate that unexpected events
can happen, and we’re always here to
support families where possible.

However, Cambridgeshire County
Council and the Department for
Education require schools to
authorise leave

only in exceptional
circumstances

—meaning rare,
unavoidable events.

Routine family holidays or planned
trips unfortunately do not meet this
threshold. You can find further
information here:

Non-attendance at school and the
law | Cambridgeshire County
Council

Thank you for your understanding
and cooperation.
